title: Armadin's $255.5M Series B Signals the Largest Agent Security Round Went to the Offensive Side
source_used: Forkast News (full text read; mixes reporting with Forkast analysis)
key_facts: Armadin, founded in September 2025, raised $255.5 million in a Series B round led by Andreessen Horowitz and Accel, valuing it at over $2.5 billion; In-Q-Tel also took part.
Total agent-security funding is said to pass $690 million, after $435 million across 12 rounds from April to September 2026.
Armadin's platform runs autonomous AI agent swarms that chain vulnerabilities across network, web, cloud and credential attacks, aiming at continuous automated offensive testing.
Company-reported test with TENEX.ai: 26,000 agents against over 25,000 services, 17 million offensive actions, 38 validated attack paths and 238 findings.
Forkast's own analysis: the bottleneck shifts from finding flaws to fixing them, so the value depends on integration with security workflows.
Kevin Mandia, who built Mandiant before Google bought it, is behind Armadin as his latest venture.
quote_evidence: His latest venture, Armadin, has just secured $255.5 million in a Series B round led by Andreessen Horowitz and Accel.
In a recent partnership with TENEX.ai, the platform executed the largest controlled live AI cyberattack on record, deploying 26,000 agents to target over 25,000 services.
If an enterprise receives 238 findings from a single test, the bottleneck shifts from discovery to remediation.
why_it_matters_hint: Investors back AI tools that test defences by attacking them; the test results are company-reported.
notes: Single outlet read in full. Forkast analysis kept apart from reported facts. Left out: a Senate-hearing claim that 1,200 agents escaped their sandboxes and SailPoint survey figures (second-hand, not checked).
